claim: Engineering non-inferiority of runtime host allocation and phase Arena against same-contract mature routes, plus scheduler guarded-stack reuse against an attested direct-VM baseline; compile-time versus runtime dispatch remains diagnostic

configuration.role: same-product direct control, not an external SOTA peer
configuration.identity: the allocator/system/fiber/scheduler implementation files are required by CMake to be byte-identical to this clean product snapshot
configuration.link_shape: candidate and direct control compile into the same executable without LTO

configuration.runtime_erasure: memory_resource provider is isolated in a separate translation unit with LTO disabled

configuration.upstream: the same HYLE runtime AllocatorRef used by candidate Arena

workloads.semantic_contract: Measure the dynamic injection tax of HYLE AllocatorRef over the exact same mimalloc-backed successful allocation batch used by compile-time SystemAllocator
workloads.setup: Both routes are warmed and share one process allocator; the direct baseline is attested source-identical to the frozen product snapshot

ownership_topology.candidate: A borrowed HYLE AllocatorRef value performs one function-pointer dispatch per successful allocate/free while preserving runtime backing identity and sized-free information
ownership_topology.peer: A borrowed oneTBB std::pmr::memory_resource pointer performs one virtual dispatch per successful allocate/free over the scalable allocator
ownership_topology.equivalence: Both warmed runtime-erased handles allocate the same 64 size/alignment pairs, expose the same live byte range, charge identical touches and reverse-order destruction, and exclude OOM from this successful steady-state row

material_contribution.derivation: The retained consumer-shapes manifest binds current runtime injection and explicitly labels the 64-item distribution as a representative north-star aggregate rather than a captured production trace

workloads.semantic_contract: Allocate, touch and reverse-free one 64-object successful host batch through a runtime-erased allocator with explicit alignment

input.distribution: 8 deterministic sizes from 24 B to 16 KiB crossed with 16/32/64-byte alignment

workloads.setup: Both process allocators and erased handles are constructed and warmed outside measurement; oneTBB's concrete resource cannot be devirtualized in the benchmark translation unit

ownership_topology.candidate: One long-lived HYLE Arena lazily grows and retains ordinary blocks across request clears while returning the 64 KiB dedicated outlier
ownership_topology.peer: One long-lived Boost monotonic resource starts at 4 KiB and releases its upstream blocks at the same bulk-invalidation boundary
ownership_topology.equivalence: Both borrow the same HYLE runtime upstream, return the same aligned writable ranges, charge the same 64 allocations/touches and bulk invalidation; retained bytes are reported separately because retention strategy is a deliberate product resource difference

material_contribution.derivation: Current http_serve owns one Arena per connection and clears after each response; the retained manifest binds its exact block policy and labels allocation sizes as a frozen request/inference distribution

workloads.semantic_contract: Serve one phase-lifetime scratch epoch with 63 ordinary allocations, one 64 KiB outlier, observable touches and one bulk invalidation

input.distribution: 63 deterministic 24 B to 8 KiB ordinary requests followed by one 64 KiB dedicated outlier

workloads.setup: Both owners and their common runtime upstream are warmed before measured epochs; owner construction and final process teardown are outside measurement
charged_phases: candidate dedicated-block return or peer release work

ownership_topology.candidate: The scheduler owns a bounded FiberStackPool; each Fiber takes one guarded stack, runs, destroys and returns it to that owner
ownership_topology.peer: The identical Scheduler/Fiber lifecycle takes a fresh guarded FiberStack mapping and destroys it directly after drain
ownership_topology.equivalence: The same source-identical Scheduler, Fiber, callback, stack size, guard semantics, spawn/drain checks and vector lifetime are charged; only warm bounded reuse versus direct VM reserve/release differs

material_contribution.derivation: The current scheduler owns exactly these stack pools and routes fiber destruction back to them; the direct route is the same public fallback for an unsupported tier

workloads.semantic_contract: Create, spawn, run, drain and destroy 16 default-tier guarded fibers with identical scheduler semantics
workloads.setup: One single-worker Scheduler is constructed outside measurement; both routes are warmed and relevant implementation files must match the frozen direct baseline
charged_phases: 16 Fiber destructions and pool returns or VM releases
